judgements.referenceQuote: is a British neuroscientist who is Vice-Chancellor of the University of Oxford and former Warden of Merton College, Oxford
judgements.rationale: The dossier separately records 'Warden (Head) of Merton College' and 'Pro-Vice Chancellor' (2018), but neither statement gives the combined fact, and the 'without portfolio' qualifier is absent, so only part of the reference fact is stated.

judgements.evidenceQuote: co-founder and director of the Oxford Centre for Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Brain (FMRIB)

judgements.referenceQuote: Her team’s research concerns the neuroscience of pain, specifically pain perception and analgesia as well as how anaesthetics produce altered states of consciousness
judgements.evidenceQuote: Professor Tracey researches the transmission of pain from the nerves in the skin to areas of the brain
judgements.rationale: The dossier covers the pain neuroscience side (also 'research into people's perception of pain'), but says nothing about analgesia, how anaesthetics produce altered states of consciousness, or multidisciplinary neuroimaging approaches, so only part of the research-area fact is stated.

usefulness.rationale: The dossier converges on a clear, well-corroborated picture of Irene Tracey: British neuroscientist (b. 30 Oct 1966), Vice-Chancellor of the University of Oxford since 1 January 2023, Professor of Anaesthetic Neuroscience, co-founder and former director of the Oxford FMRIB centre, former Warden of Merton College (installed 5 Oct 2019), with a full career timeline (Harvard postdoc 1994–96, Oxford lectureship 2001, FMRIB director 2005–2015, Nuffield Chair 2007–2019, head of department 2016–2019) drawn from Wikipedia, Oxford Podcasts, an ORCID self-report, and Crossref records. Her research focus (pain transmission, brain-stem modulation, the 'good cop/bad cop' signals) and recent authorships are documented. Notably, none of the three listed unjustified conclusions (New England Biolabs/Tufts, Lancet authorship, sole-founder) appears as a dossier statement — the founding claims correctly say 'helped to found' and 'co-founder' — so no overclaims are warranted. The dossier is weakened as a record of its own uncertainty by roughly ten placeholder 'statement' claims with contested status that convey nothing, and by a block of supported claims about entirely different people (Steven Gunn, Chris Patten) that inflates the dossier without adding Tracey evidence; confidence signalling is present via status fields but open questions are never articulated. A reader could still prepare well for a meeting: current role, career history, expertise, honours (CBE, FRS, FMedSci), and recent publications are all covered.
